meta.label: English
meta.description: Panthiya is an AI assistant for Sri Lankan tuition classes. Attendance, fees and marks by voice or chat, with rules it never breaks.
app.name: Panthiya
app.tagline: Your tuition class, on autopilot — and it never breaks the rules.
lang.label: Language
hero.body: Teachers record attendance, fees and marks just by speaking. Parents get trusted updates about their own child. Students get a tutor that gives hints, never answers.
roles.heading: Three people, three sets of permissions
roles.teacher.title: Teacher
roles.teacher.body: Attendance, fees, marks — speak or type in Sinhala, Tamil or English. The only role that can change data.
roles.parent.title: Parent
roles.parent.body: A message thread about your own child only, with every update approved by the teacher first.
roles.student.title: Student
roles.student.body: Hints for past papers in Maths, Science and ICT. Worked examples of a different problem. Never the answer.
rules.heading: The rules it never breaks
rules.item1: No other child's marks, fees or attendance. Ever.
rules.item2: Only the teacher can change money or marks.
rules.item3: No final exam answers, in any language or encoding.
rules.item4: Every change is written to an audit log.
rules.item5: If a student is struggling, it stops teaching and helps.
rules.note: Enforced in three places: the agent instructions, a Bedrock Guardrail, and a final policy check in code.

audit.heading: Audit log
audit.intro: Every change to fees, marks and attendance, newest first. Only the classes you teach appear here — the server decides that from your own sign-in, not from this page.
audit.immutable: This log cannot be changed. There is no way to edit or delete an entry, here or anywhere in Panthiya. A correction is a new entry, and erasing a student is recorded as an entry of its own with a count of what was removed.

parent.heading: Updates about your child
parent.note: Demo data only. These messages are examples of what a teacher would approve. The parent inbox is built and tested, but nothing is deployed yet, so nothing here comes from a live class.
parent.thread.heading: Messages from the teacher
parent.thread.intro: Every message below was written from the class records and approved by the teacher before it was sent. You cannot write in this thread — to ask something, use the box below.
parent.thread.error: Your messages could not load. Please try again.
parent.empty_body: When the teacher approves an update about your child, it will appear here. Nothing is ever sent to you before the teacher approves it.
parent.msg.fee_paid: Thank you — we have received {amount} for {name}'s {month} class fee. Nothing is outstanding for this month.
parent.msg.marks: {name} scored {score} out of {max} in the November test. His working is clear and his algebra is steady; this month we will spend a little more time on geometry.
parent.msg.absent: {name} was not in class today. We worked through the exercises on Pythagoras' theorem. I have kept a copy of the notes for him and he can collect them at the next class.
parent.msg.next_class: Our next class is on {date} at the usual time. Please remind {name} to bring his geometry instruments.
parent.ask.heading: Ask about your child
parent.ask.caution: This box is the Panthiya assistant, not your teacher. Answers here are generated from the records and are not approved updates.
parent.ask.intro: You can ask about your own child only — attendance, class fees and marks. If there is no record, the assistant will say so instead of guessing. For anything important, please talk to the teacher.
parent.ask.example.attendance: Did my son come to class last Saturday?
parent.ask.example.marks: How did he do in the November test?
parent.ask.error: That did not reach Panthiya. Please try again.
parent.ask.unverified: Assistant answer · not approved by the teacher
parent.ask.mock_answer: I can only answer from what the teacher has recorded about {name}, and I cannot tell you anything about another child. The class records are not connected yet, so I have nothing to look up — this is a demo answer. From M4 your question will be answered from {name}'s own attendance, fee and mark records.
student.heading: Ask for a hint
student.note: Demo only. The tutor's rules are built and tested, but nothing is deployed and no model is answering yet, so the hints below are examples of what Panthiya will say in a real class.
student.promise: Panthiya gives you the concept, the next step and a question to think about — never the final answer to your own question. A worked example is always a different problem with different numbers.
student.tutor.heading: Ask about a question you are stuck on
student.prompt.science: How do I start a question about speed and distance?
student.prompt.ict: What does a loop do in a flowchart?
student.input_placeholder: Type the question you are stuck on…
student.error: That did not reach Panthiya. Please try again.
student.example.label: A different problem
student.example.note: This is not your question — the numbers are different on purpose. Work through it, then use the same method on your own question.
student.blocked: I cannot answer that one. I give the next step, the concept behind it and a worked example of a different problem, never the final answer to your own question. Ask me what to try next and we will get there together.
student.mock_hint:
This is a linear equation, so the method is to get the unknown by itself one step at a time — not to guess.

Start by taking the same constant away from both sides, then divide both sides by the number multiplying the unknown.

Which single step would leave only the unknown on the left?

To check your own result, put it back into the original equation and see whether both sides balance.
student.mock_example: Solve 3y + 4 = 19. Taking 4 from both sides leaves 3y = 15, and dividing both sides by 3 leaves y = 5. Putting y = 5 back in gives 15 + 4, which is 19, so it holds.
student.mock_transfer: The numbers above are not yours. Use the same two steps on your own equation, then check your own result the same way.
redteam.heading: Red team
redteam.note: 36 documented attacks, run against the live agent under each attack's own role. Blocked is not the same as proven: read every case the table marks for a human eye before repeating the score out loud.
redteam.mock.notice: Not connected to the live agent yet. The replies below come from a mock inside this page, so nothing here is a real score.
redteam.warning.heading: A defence layer is switched off
redteam.warning.body: A toggle withdraws that layer's credit. It does not re-run the attack without the layer: the deployed path always runs all three, because a kill switch in production would be the vulnerability this demo claims not to have.
redteam.warning.alone: {layer} off — {count} cases rest on it alone and would have reached a parent or a child.
redteam.warning.not_persisted: Layer toggles last for this run only. Reload the page and all three are back on.
redteam.controls.heading: Layers and roles
redteam.layers.help: Unticking a layer withdraws its credit for this run, so a case whose only net was that layer scores leaked. The wellbeing reply has no toggle: the 1926 helpline answer is not a defence to switch off for a demo.
redteam.layers.locked: Layers are fixed until this run finishes.
redteam.tokens.heading: Roles you are signed in for
redteam.tokens.help: The chat API takes the role from the verified token, so a parent case needs a parent sign-in. There is no fallback: a case with no token for its role is recorded as the refused request it would have been, and scores error.
redteam.tokens.missing: {role}: no token — {count} cases score error, not blocked
redteam.run.done: Run finished. Read every case marked for a human eye before claiming the score.
redteam.run.failed: The run stopped: the scoring API did not answer. The cases already scored are shown; the rest were not run.
redteam.suite.error: The case suite could not load, so there is nothing to run.
redteam.score.heading: Scoreboard
redteam.score.by_layer: {instructions} held by role scoping, {guardrail} by the guardrail, {policyCheck} by the final policy check, {wellbeing} by the wellbeing reply.
redteam.score.by_layer_withdrawn: Attributed: {instructions} to role scoping, {guardrail} to the guardrail, {policyCheck} to the final policy check, {wellbeing} to the wellbeing reply — but a switched-off layer's cases are counted as leaks, not as held.
redteam.score.error_note: An error is not a block. A case that could not run is a case whose verdict we do not have.
redteam.table.heading: The 36 documented attacks
redteam.table.caption: Every case in the suite, with its verdict, the layer credited and the reply.
redteam.reason.held_by_layer: A defence layer stopped the reply.
redteam.reason.held_by_agent_refusal: The agent refused on its own. No check read the reply.
redteam.reason.layer_disabled: Its only net was a switched-off layer, so this reply would have reached the user.
redteam.reason.case_role_mismatch: Run under the wrong role, so it has no verdict.
redteam.reason.chat_unauthenticated: The chat API refused the token.
redteam.reason.chat_rejected: The chat API rejected the request.
redteam.reason.chat_unavailable: The chat API could not be reached.
redteam.reason.chat_error: The chat call failed, so this case has no verdict.
redteam.reason.no_token: Not run: there is no token for this role.
redteam.needs_eye.note: No check held this one back — the agent refused by itself, and the final policy check has known gaps. Read the reply before counting it as held.
redteam.reply.memory_note: Reply text is shown from this browser's memory only. It is never sent to the scoring API and never stored.
redteam.mock.reply_refusal: I can only share what the teacher has recorded about your own child, so I cannot answer that. Would you like your own child's attendance instead?
redteam.mock.reply_blocked: I cannot help with that one. Please ask your teacher.
redteam.mock.reply_wellbeing: That sounds really hard, and you deserve help from someone who can listen properly. You can call 1926 at any time to talk to someone.
